chief_complaint: massive, firm, pruritic overgrowth of scar tissue extending far beyond original ear piercing site
hpi_details: 23F presenting with large, dumbbell-shaped lobular keloids on bilateral earlobes resistant to conservative therapy undergoing surgical core excision followed immediately by adjuvant intralesional triamcinolone acetonide injections and pressure earrings.
ideas: She thinks her earlobes had a severe allergic reaction to the metal in her piercings that triggered an ongoing trapped infection and caused abnormal scar tissue to swell up.
concerns: She is deeply self-conscious about people staring at her ears at work and worries that cutting the bumps off will only make them grow back even larger and more disfiguring.
expectations: She hopes the doctor can safely remove the lumps or give her an injection today so her ears look normal again and she can stop hiding her hair.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Bilateral Earlobe Keloids evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Bilateral Earlobe Keloids is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Bilateral Earlobe Keloids, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Bilateral Earlobe Keloids.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Flap ischemia or tissue necrosis.
management_principles: Surgical core (intramarginal) excision with immediate adjuvant intralesional triamcinolone acetonide and continuous pressure earrings, plus scheduled repeat injections and long-term recurrence surveillance
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

history.answer: I came in because huge, firm lumps have grown on both of my earlobes right where I had them pierced.
I got both ears pierced about a year ago, and these lumps started showing up about eight or nine months ago.
They are on both of my earlobes, surrounding the piercing sites and wrapping around from front to back like dumbbells.
They started off as tiny bumps, but they have grown steadily over several months and spread well past the initial piercing holes.
There is one large growth on each earlobe, making two in total. I do not have any lumps anywhere else on my body.
They feel very hard and rubbery, like dense cartilage, and they stay attached to the earlobe rather than slipping around underneath the skin.
They do not hurt on their own, but they feel mildly sore and tender if I press firmly on them or sleep directly on my sides.
Yes, they itch quite often, especially when the room gets warm or if my hair rubs against them.
No, neither lump looks like a mole, and I have not noticed any new dark spots or changing moles anywhere on my skin.
No, they have never cracked open, bled, or formed scabs.
No, there is no redness, swelling, heat, pus, or bad odor coming from my earlobes.
No, there is no central dark pore or hole, and nothing cheesy or white comes out even if I squeeze them.
No, their size does not fluctuate; they never shrink back down and have only grown larger over time.
This all started after I got my earlobes pierced at an accessory boutique a year ago. I have not had any other cuts, surgeries, or acne on my ears.
I applied over-the-counter silicone scar gel and adhesive sheets daily for about two months, but they did not help at all and the lumps kept enlarging.
No, I have had no fever, chills, night sweats, unintended weight loss, or swollen glands.
I work indoors and wear sunscreen when outside, and I have never had a blistering sunburn.
No, neither I nor anyone in my family has ever had melanoma or any other form of skin cancer.
No, I have never taken immunosuppressive medications, never had an organ transplant, and do not have diabetes.
I'm so embarrassed by how noticeable they are at work, and I'm terrified that if you cut them off, they'll just grow back twice as big and ruin my ears completely.
I thought my ears must have had a bad allergic reaction to the cheap metal earrings I used, or that an infection got trapped inside the piercing holes and made the tissue swell out of control.
I'm so embarrassed by how noticeable they are at work, and I'm terrified that if you cut them off, they'll just grow back twice as big and ruin my ears completely.
I'm hoping you can shave these lumps off or give me an injection today so my ears look normal again and I don't have to keep wearing my hair down to hide them.
I have no chronic medical conditions such as high blood pressure, asthma, or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital stays in my life, aside from the ear piercings.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
My mother told me she also tends to develop thick, raised scars whenever she gets cuts or incisions.
I have never smoked cigarettes, and I only have an occasional glass of wine once or twice a month.
I work full-time as an office administrator and share an apartment with a roommate.
My last period started two weeks ago, my monthly cycles are completely regular, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.
I am not currently sexually active and I do not use any birth control pills or implants.
